title: Ammeter readings table
subject: Science
source: Seeded from science/y7 lesson 33 (Ammeter readings table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 33: Measuring current with an ammeter. To understand how to measure current and what happens to it in a series circuit

questions.q: Draw a series circuit with a cell, a lamp and an ammeter.
questions.a: One loop with cell, lamp and A-in-a-circle
questions.model: One loop only. Put the ammeter in the loop like any other component: cell, wire, ammeter, wire, lamp, wire back.

questions.q: Two lamps in series: A1 reads 0.25 A. What does A2 read?
What happens to the current if you add a second cell?
In the simulator, build a series circuit with two lamps and three ammeters. Record the readings, then add a cell and record again.
questions.a: All three readings equal; all increase when a cell is added (exact values depend on the simulator)
questions.model: Teacher places the first ammeter on screen and reads it aloud: '0.30 A.'

questions.q: Explain why the lamps are dimmer with two in series than one.
questions.a: Two lamps give more resistance, so the current is smaller.

questions.q: Why must an ammeter have very low resistance?
questions.a: So it does not reduce the current it is measuring.

questions.q: Big question: is current bigger, smaller or the same after a lamp?
questions.a: The same: current is not used up in a series circuit.
